description: Combine the compact n=512 plus aliased right-looking n=2048 global-best stack with the many-CTA blocked n=1024 TRSM winner. Import only n=1024 coalesced panel tiles, four-stage 64-wide forward solves, 720/480/240-CTA launch state, and workspace binding while preserving the profiled padded factor kernel, epoch publication, deterministic n=256, n=128 WMMA, compact bulk/mbarrier n=512, aliased n=2048 operands, large dispatches, caches, fresh inputs, and the full grid.

Imported only Brief49's many-CTA batch60/n1024 panel solve into Brief60's compact-n512/aliased-right-looking-n2048 stack: coalesced 64-row panel tiles, four 64-wide MathDx forward-solve stages, LD68/LD72 shared operands, cached caller-queue/output views, and 720/480/240-CTA launches. The first parent's profiled padded factor kernel, epoch publication, n128/n256/n512/n2048 paths, caches, and large dispatches remain unchanged. This directly replaces the exact hosted index-7 capture's 137.76 us cuBLAS TRSM (1440 blocks, 62.28% occupancy) while retaining its factor path; Brief60's parent evidence was n2048 panel 157.18 us, 56 registers, 12.48% occupancy, 92.30% no-eligible cycles, and 63.01% CTA-barrier stalls. Slice-wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Batch60/n1024 improved from first-parent 1484.459 to 1033.804 us; batch640/n512 measured 968.926 us, batch8/n2048 1880.205 us, and aggregate improved from 844.188 to 824.561 us. Hosted profiling is still centrally reserved and was not consumed without manager grant.

Held the exact four-stage 64-wide blocked batch1024 solve, LD68/LD72 shared layout, coalesced panel mapping, 720/480/240 grids, factor/epoch kernel, and all other Brief60 paths fixed while doubling each panel CTA from 256 to 512 threads. Slice-wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1065.154 us versus 1033.804 for 256 threads; aggregate measured 834.068 versus 824.561, with broadly slower unrelated cells in this sample. The measured 256-thread integration remains the lower target-cell result.

Restored the measured 256-thread many-CTA panel width and changed only both FP16 forward-update operands from LD72 to aligned LD80, retaining LD68 FP32 tiles, the four 64-wide solves, 720/480/240 launch grids, first-parent factor/epoch state, and every other dispatch. Slice-wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full 15-cell grid passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1083.836 us versus 1033.804 for LD72; aggregate measured 837.182 versus 824.561 in another broadly slower system sample. LD72 remains the lower measured target-cell layout.

Restored the target-winning 256-thread LD68/LD72 panel path and fused all 36 live triangular compact-factor scatter tiles into each nonterminal panel launch, removing the separate 64-tile scatter/pointer launch while preserving the factor kernel, epoch state, four-stage solve, output cache, and every other dispatch. The fused launch used 2880/2640/2400 total CTAs across scatter plus solve work. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1099.389 us versus 1033.804 for separate scatter plus solve; aggregate measured 829.636 versus 824.561. The fused scatter CTAs share the panel kernel's 52 KiB dynamic allocation, leaving a separate compact scatter kernel as an open variant.

Separated the compact-factor scatter back out of the large-shared panel solve, but replaced the 64-tile C++ grid with an exact 36-live-tile, 4.125 KiB-shared Numba launch before each 720/480/240-CTA solve. This removes 1680 immediate-return blocks per stage and pointer writes while keeping coalesced transpose staging, the 256-thread LD68/LD72 solver, factor/epoch kernel, and all other Brief60 paths unchanged. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1043.412 us versus 1033.804 for the imported C++ scatter; aggregate measured 827.045 versus 824.561, quantifying the live-tile split as close but slower in this sample.

Returned to the trial0 256-thread LD68/LD72 solver with the original coalesced C++ factor scatter, then merged each 64x64 output-panel load with its read-only diagonal-factor load into one cooperative loop and one shared barrier. This removes one CTA-wide barrier from each of the four forward-solve stages without changing operands, MathDx operators, 720/480/240 grids, factor/epoch publication, or other dispatches. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch60/n1024 improved from 1033.804 to 1011.399 us; aggregate measured 824.608 versus 824.561 because the unrelated n32768 cell sampled 53123.508 versus 52687.738 us. The combined loader is the lower measured n1024 result.

Extended the combined panel/diagonal loader to also stage the first prior-factor and prior-panel FP16 update pair for k>0, removing a second shared barrier from three of the four 64-wide forward-solve stages while retaining the same math and grids. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed correctness. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1011.399 to 1273.181 us and aggregate measured 845.242 versus 824.608 in a broadly slower sample; the wider live loader materially increased the target path despite fewer barriers.

Returned to the target-winning combined panel/diagonal loader and halved only the many-CTA solve width from 256 to 128 threads, increasing per-thread cooperative loads while testing whether the 52 KiB shared footprint could admit more blocks and recover occupancy. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch60/n1024 regressed from 1011.399 to 1381.329 us; aggregate measured 854.075 versus 824.608 in a slower system sample. Together with the measured 512-thread 1065.154 us variant, 256 threads is the lower measured panel width.

Restored 256-thread panels while retaining the widened panel/diagonal/first-update co-loader, then increased only its FP32 accumulator and triangular stride from LD68 to LD72. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all benchmark cells passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1334.801 us versus 1273.181 for the widened LD68 loader and 1011.399 for the narrower combined LD68 loader; aggregate measured 855.199 us in a broadly slower sample. This isolates additional regression from the FP32 LD72 layout on top of the already costly wider live loader.

Used the exact Trial5 hosted index7 profile to attack the panel kernel's measured 53.25 KiB one-block shared limit, 96 registers/thread, 12.47% occupancy, 62.03% no-eligible cycles, and 270.24 us first-stage duration. Aliased the diagonal FP32 tile over the no-longer-live pair of FP16 update tiles, delayed diagonal loading until updates completed, and used LD64 throughout to reduce dynamic shared memory to exactly 32 KiB, permitting two blocks per 64 KiB shared configuration. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1211.682 us versus 1011.399 for LD68/LD72, and aggregate measured 834.559 versus 824.608; the reduced footprint incurred a larger measured cost from the compact layouts.

Retained profile-proven LD68 FP32 and LD72 FP16 bank-skew layouts, but aliased the two FP16 update operands with the later-live diagonal FP32 tile and requested a 100% shared carveout. This reduced panel dynamic shared memory from the hosted capture's 53.25 KiB one-block limit to 35 KiB while avoiding Trial9's compact-LD64 penalty, enabling two resident CTAs under the profiled 96-register limit. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full 15-cell grid passed. Batch60/n1024 improved from Trial5 1011.399 to 950.307 us (best 945.152), and aggregate improved from 824.608 to a new brief/global low 821.454 us. The exact hosted profile motivating this edit is canonicalized under brief-61-trial-5-20a8ef1a456b7aeac2b3a6291650a41ab7bcae5b.*.

Held the 35 KiB aliased padded LD68/LD72 panel workspace fixed and reduced only the preferred shared-memory carveout from 100% to 75%, testing whether the same two-CTA residency could retain more L1 capacity after the hosted capture measured 40.56% L1 hit rate. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 951.901 us versus 950.307 at 100% (best 947.136 versus 945.152); aggregate measured 822.066 versus 821.454 amid slower unrelated large cells. The 100% setting remains the lower measured result.

Restored the 100% carveout and doubled only the 35 KiB aliased padded panel kernel from 256 to 512 threads, testing whether the reduced shared footprint could combine two-CTA residency with more warps than the original 53.25 KiB layout. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 1020.795 us versus 950.307 for 256 threads, and aggregate measured 833.296 versus 821.454 in a broadly slower sample. The aliased 256-thread configuration remains lower.

Restored 256-thread aliased panels at 100% carveout and increased only the FP32 triangular/accumulator stride from LD68 to LD72 while retaining FP16 LD72 and two-CTA-capable 36 KiB shared footprint. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all cells passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 961.554 us versus 950.307 for FP32 LD68, and aggregate measured 823.338 versus 821.454 amid slower unrelated cells. Padded FP32 LD68 remains the lower measured aliased layout.

Returned to the Trial10 256-thread FP32-LD68/FP16-LD72 alias and 100% carveout, then co-loaded the k0 panel and diagonal factor into disjoint shared views before the workspace becomes aliased by later updates, removing one barrier only from the first of four forward-solve stages. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 959.425 us versus 950.307 for separate k0 loads, although its best sample was 941.056 versus 945.152; aggregate measured 829.370 versus 821.454 in a broadly slower system sample. Separate loading remains the lower mean result.

Returned to separate-load 256-thread panels with FP32 LD68 and 100% carveout, then increased only aliased FP16 update operands from LD72 to aligned LD80, expanding shared footprint from 35 to 37 KiB while retaining two-CTA-capable residency. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Batch60/n1024 measured 964.220 us versus 950.307 for LD72, and aggregate measured 823.050 versus 821.454. LD72 remains the lower measured aliased operand stride.

Restored the exact Trial10 FP32-LD68/FP16-LD72, 256-thread, 35 KiB aliased workspace with 100% carveout after the completed stride/width sweep. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and full grid passed. Under a systemically noisy run, identical source measured batch60/n1024 1051.422 us (best 965.472) and aggregate 840.532 versus its earlier 950.307 us (best 945.152) and 821.454 aggregate; unrelated n256/n512/n2048 cells also regressed substantially. Commit 32e8f3e remains the lower exact-source measurement, while this commit records the clean restored source state.

Combined Brief49's hosted-profile-motivated many-CTA n1024 solve into Brief60's compact-n512/aliased-n2048 stack and ran 17 fully committed trials. Trial0 ab51eb6 imported exact coalesced 64-row tiles, four 64-wide MathDx solves, LD68/LD72 operands, cached output/queue state, and 720/480/240 CTAs while preserving the first-parent factor/epoch kernel and every other path; it measured 824.561 us aggregate and 1033.804 us at batch60/n1024 versus parent 844.188/1484.459. Trial5 20a8ef1 co-loaded panel/diagonal tiles and reached 824.608/1011.399. The one authorized hosted index7 request profiled exact 20a8ef1: job 76f1dc20b0a24ee5b92608e6222e7fc4 at 2026-07-19T23:58:49Z; canonical brief-61-trial-5-20a8ef1a456b7aeac2b3a6291650a41ab7bcae5b artifacts show panel stage0 270.24 us, 720x256, 96 registers/thread, 53.25 KiB dynamic shared, one block/SM, 12.47% occupancy, 62.03% no-eligible, and a 128-block tail; retained factor measured 201.09 us, 168 registers, 6.25% occupancy, 89.96% no-eligible. Profile-driven Trial10 32e8f3ea47ea0c15cea9f7131a72ca544d95f452 aliases padded LD68/LD72 update workspace with the later-live diagonal and requests full shared carveout, cutting footprint to 35 KiB while avoiding LD64 conflicts; all checks passed and it reached the brief/global low 821.454 us, batch60/n1024 950.307 us (best 945.152). Exact-source restoration fe2abbb also passed but sampled 840.532 under fleet-wide slowdown, so 32e8f3e carries the lower evidence. Measured alternatives: 512-thread 1065.154 before alias and 1020.795 after; 128-thread 1381.329; FP16 LD80 1083.836 before alias and 964.220 after; FP32 LD72 alias 961.554; 75% carveout 951.901; compact LD64 two-block alias 1211.682; fused scatter 1099.389; live-tile split scatter 1043.412; widened co-loader 1273.181; k0 co-load 959.425. Keep the work moving: stage-specific panel operators/carveouts, lowering the profiled 96 registers without losing padded banks, software-pipelined/asynchronous panel-factor staging inside the 35 KiB budget, and residency-aware tail scheduling for the 720/480/240 grids remain concrete follow-ups. No second hosted request was issued.
